selection_reasoning: The 'find melon' task is a straightforward visual search task that requires the agent to locate a melon block in the Minecraft environment. It is observable and verifiable (the agent needs to navigate to and look at a melon block), does not require deep Minecraft domain knowledge, and can be set up in a scene with clear visual landmarks. As a single atomic task, no dependency chain is needed, but it provides a clean, verifiable benchmark for navigation and object recognition.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because 'find melon' is a locate/observe task — the player must navigate close enough to the melon block and face toward it, modeling 'the player can see the melon.' The melon is at (7, 1, -7) spawn-relative, approximately 10 blocks from spawn and behind the player's initial facing direction (blocked by an oak shed). max_distance=5 ensures the player must walk at least ~5 blocks toward the melon (cannot be satisfied at spawn since spawn-to-melon distance is ~10). facing_tolerance=45 ensures the player is genuinely looking at the melon, not just nearby facing a random direction.

scene_description: A farm scene where the player spawns facing an oak planks shed that blocks their initial view. The melon is placed behind the player at (7, 1, -7) on farmland, requiring the player to turn around and explore. Pumpkin distractors are placed in visible areas to test visual discrimination. Hay bales, a chicken, fencing, and a composter add farm ambiance.
task_text: Find the melon block in the farm scene.
design_notes: The melon is at (7, 1, -7) spawn-relative — about 10 blocks from spawn, behind the player and to the right. The oak planks shed at (±2, 0-2, 3-5) blocks the initial forward view. The player must turn around (~180°) and walk toward the farmland area to find the melon. Pumpkins at (5,1,-5) and (3,0,2) serve as visual distractors. The scene is 20x20 blocks on a grass platform.
